steps.ask: Which quadrants make cosine positive, and how many full turns does 2X cover?

lines.text: $\cos$ is positive in the 1st and 4th quadrants. Since $0^\circ \le X \le 360^\circ$, we need $0^\circ \le \hl{2}{2X} \le 720^\circ$, which is two full turns.
First turn: $\hl{2}{2X} = \hl{2}{30^\circ}$ or $360^\circ - 30^\circ = \hl{2}{330^\circ}$.
Second turn: add $360^\circ$ to each, giving $\hl{2}{390^\circ}$ and $\hl{2}{690^\circ}$.

steps.ask: If θ = 3x, over what range does θ run, and in which quadrants is sine positive?
steps.title: Find the angles whose sine is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

lines.text: Let $\hl{2}{\theta}=\hl{2}{3x}$. Since $0\le x\le 360$, we need $0\le \hl{2}{\theta}\le 1080$.

$\sin\hl{2}{\theta}=\hl{1}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}$ has reference angle $\hl{4}{60^\circ}$. Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants, so $\hl{2}{\theta}=\hl{2}{60^\circ}$ or $\hl{2}{\theta}=180^\circ-60^\circ=\hl{2}{120^\circ}$.
Add $360^\circ$ repeatedly to stay inside the range.
